thread.title: Stocks, Dow Jones Rally; Meet Tesla's No. 2 Shareholder | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks, Dow Jones Rally; Meet Tesla's No. 2 Shareholder | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks jumped, then pared some early gains Tuesday as two small cap benchmarks climbed back above the bear market boundary.
X Cree ( CREE ) led the early gains among chip stocks. Tesla ( TSLA ) stock aimed to extend its rally, after Larry Ellison doubled his stake in the company to $1 billion. Twilio ( TWLO ) targeted a new high, jumping on a price target hike. Union Pacific ( UNP ) surged after announcing a new chief operating officer. Carnival Cruise ( CCL ) jumped following a Florida court ruling.
The Dow Jones industrial average powered up 1.2% at the starting bell. Boeing ( BA ) jumped 2.4% to lead the Dow.
S&P 500 futures were up 0.9% and just off early highs. Union Pacific led the index. PG&E Corp. ( PCG ) held its worst decline.
The Nasdaq Composite also popped, then eased off highs, gaining 0.8%, with Monster Beverage ( MNST ) running at the head of the Nasdaq 100. Illumina ( ILMN ) lagged at the bottom the Nasdaq 100.

The S&P 500 has gained 8.7%, also from a Dec. 26 bottom. The Nasdaq has soared 10.2% off its low from Dec. 24. That leaves the Nasdaq less than 3% below a key test of resistance at its 50-day moving average . The S&P 500 is also about 3% from its 50-day, while the Dow is 4% below the line.
Small Caps Exit Bear Market The S&P Smallcap 600 lagged the general market, up 0.6% in early trade. But that was enough to narrow its loss from an August high to less than 20%, effectively hoisting it above the bear market threshold for the first time since mid-December.
The Russell 2000, another leading small cap benchmark rose 0.9% Tuesday. IT had exited bear market status on Monday.
Tesla Stock: Ellison, Musk Largest Shareholders Tesla stock gained 2% in early trade. Oracle ( ORCL ) founder Larry Ellison reported he owned 3 million shares, a 1.75% stake worth $1 billion, in the company. That makes him the second largest shareholder, after Chief Executive Elon Musk. Ellison joined Tesla's board of directors in December.
Tesla stock vaulted 5.4% higher on Monday. The stock is shaping a possible new base after a failed breakout in December triggered the automatic sell rule.
Shutdown, Day 17: Presidential Blitz As the shutdown of federal offices and agencies enters its 17th day, no potential budget compromise was yet in sight. Domestic politics continued to dominate, but trade-sensitive stock futures also received a boost from a presidential tweet, announcing "Talks with China are going very well!," referring to negotiations underway between U.S. and Chinese trade officials in Beijing.
The White House on Monday launched what Roll Call described as a presidential public relations blitz, in the battle with House Democrats for $5.7 billion in funding to build a wall at the southern U.S. border. President Trump will deliver his first-ever prime time Oval Office address Tuesday night and plans to visit the southern border on Thursday. The $5.7 billion is part of $7 billion in new funds sought for Homeland Security. The president is considering invoking the National Emergencies Act of 1976 in order to appropriate the funding he seeks.
On Monday, Trump administration lawyers broke precedent and ruled the Internal Revenue Service, effectively operating on a skeleton staff, could process and deliver tax refunds during the shutdown. Last year, the IRS paid more than $147 billion in tax refunds to 48.5 million households from Jan. 29 to March 2, according to the Washington Post.
Chip Stocks Up, Despite Samsung Chip stocks traded generally higher early Tuesday, despite a revenue and earnings miss by South Korea's Samsung. The electronics giant reported that tariff-slowed trade between the U.S. and China had hit its memory chip business hard, echoing the December-quarter report last month from Apple ( AAPL ).
Cree surged to the head of the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, up 4.1% after announcing a multi-year silicon carbide wafer supply agreement with ST Microelectronics ( STM ). ST Micro gained 2.1% at the open. Cree is trading below a 47.60 buy point in a cup-with-handle base.
Advanced Micro Devices rolled 1% higher. The stock is working on its third weekly advance, and has been shaping a bottom to its consolidation since early November. Shares jumped back above their 50-day moving average in an 8% surge on Monday.
Oil Prices Extend Advance Oil prices continued higher Tuesday, with West Texas Intermediate up 1.8%, pressing toward $50 a barrel and working on its eighth straight advance. WTI has gained 14.5% since Dec. 24, partly on an agreement between Russia and the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries to trim production. On Monday, the Wall Street Journal reported Saudi Arabia planned to sharply curtail oil exports beginning this month, effectively more than doubling the 3% output cut (vs. October levels) it pledged in the OPEC-Russia arrangement. The Saudis are reportedly targeting an $80 price for Brent crude. Brent rose 1.7% early Tuesday, to $58.30.
Stocks: Twilio, Monster Get Price Hikes Cloud-based software leader Twilio gave up an opening gain and slipped 0.4% after KeyBanc notched up the stock's price target to 114, from 103. The brokerage maintained the stock's overweight rating. Shares had swept nearly 10% higher on Monday, retaking an 88.98 buy point in a cup base. Twilio's initial breakout from that base, in November, had failed — falling more than 8% below the buy point and triggering the automatic sell rule . The stock had moved beyond the buy point's buy range on Monday.
Monster Beverage rolled 5% higher after SunTrust Robinson Humphrey upgraded the stock to buy, from hold. The note also hoisted the stock's price target to 65, from 50. Monster shares have been in a deepening downtrend since February.
